source: Independently authored local fixture against the actual stackd CLI using SigV4 boto3 HTTP requests; not an AWS capture
checks: Fresh SQLite controller uses its STS-observed random account identity.
Signed user requests enforce group policies, a permissions boundary, object and bucket resource scope, and s3:prefix listing conditions.
Changing the attached managed policy default version denies an existing user's ranged GET; restoring the default version allows it.
Removing group membership denies an existing user's ranged GET; restoring membership allows it.
Signed assumed-role requests enforce object and bucket scope and reject unrelated prefixes.
Changing an existing role's inline policy immediately denies the existing session; restoring its policy allows it.
Deleting and recreating the role produces a distinct RoleId, denies the stale session with AccessDenied, and permits a newly assumed session.
Binary ranged GET returns HTTP 206, exact selected bytes, Content-Range, Content-Length, matching ETag and AES256 metadata.
User and role prefix listing each returns all seven expected keys in four ordered pages without duplicates or unrelated keys.
Graceful SIGTERM and controller restart retain every pre-stop kernel_events and api_call_events row unchanged within the persisted sequence prefix.
HTTP response request IDs correlate to durable journal operation names, exact error codes and observed S3 HTTP statuses.
After restart, the user key and replacement role session still read the binary range, while the stale role session remains denied.
After restart, a complete root inventory retains all 59 keys and a full GET retains the exact independently authored binary payload.
boundaries: This fixture establishes observed local CLI behavior, not AWS cloud conformance or a performance comparison.
No private worktree, resource name or payload was consulted; public evidence contains only sanitized assertions, versions and observed quantities.
The private SQLite fixture and detailed request-correlation evidence remain under the ignored runtime directory.
